# NVIDIA Kubernetes Definition (NKD) v1

***Note:** This is a long doc, fleshing out design details from* [NKD Product Proposal \+ Requirements](https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1gwnlSggRGriXN1Zl9rkHtExs2904HfGETtLqe4LEChI/edit) *doc. ## 1\. TLDR; {#1.-tldr;}

NKD defines the Kubernetes software configuration that NVIDIA validates for NKE and provides the reproducible pipeline that materializes that definition. NVIDIA runs the pipeline first, once for each supported builder profile, builds canonical reference artifacts, and validates those artifacts. It publishes the definition, pipeline, signed builder profiles, expected artifact identities, and validation evidence, but it **does not distribute the built artifacts themselves**.

NVIDIA publishes and maintains:

- a versioned, immutable definition of the Kubernetes, operating-system, and accelerated-runtime inputs validated with NKE\
- a versioned, CI-portable pipeline and signed builder profiles that deterministically turn the definition into deployable artifacts\
- cryptographic identities, SBOMs, provenance, and validation results for NVIDIA's internal reference build under each supported builder profile\
- a Kubernetes conformance claim for each released definition, with supporting evidence and an operator-runnable validation suite\
- compatibility evidence for the definition and NKE\
- lifecycle guidance and updates when versions, dependencies, or security fixes change

The operator copies or imports the released pipeline into its own CI environment, selects a supported builder profile, and runs it with the exact pinned inputs. A correct reproduction under that profile produces canonical artifacts byte-for-byte identical to NVIDIA's reference artifacts for the same profile. The operator verifies the result against NVIDIA-published digests, adds its own signatures and registry metadata outside the canonical byte boundary, promotes the artifacts, bootstraps NKE, and operates the fleet. NKE consumes the artifacts but does not build them. Where a host-level difference makes an exact byte match impossible, a tightly gated ValidatedVariant path applies: it carries its own identity and never claims byte reproduction.

## 2\. Status and interpretation {#2.-status-and-interpretation}

This document formalizes the product direction in [NKD Product Proposal \+ Requirements Document](https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1gwnlSggRGriXN1Zl9rkHtExs2904HfGETtLqe4LEChI/edit) doc. It distinguishes among:

- **product decisions** already established by the vision\
- **v1 requirements** necessary to make those decisions operable\
- **open decisions** that must be resolved before a supported external release

This design resolves the proposal's delivery ambiguity: 1\) NVIDIA builds and validates an internal canonical release set under every supported builder profile, but does not make those bytes available to end users. 2\) An operator runs the same released recipe and pipeline under a declared profile. The takeaways is that the exact matches are Reproduced; approved semantic equivalents are separately identified ValidatedVariants; all other deviations are unsupported variants or forks.

## 3\. Context and problem statement {#3.-context-and-problem-statement}

NKE instantiates a management-plane and tenant workload clusters in an AI Factory. It requires a compatible set of:

- NKE management controllers\
- Kubernetes control-plane and data-plane components\
- Core runtime components\
- AICR components, including the GPU and network stacks

Without NKD, an operator must discover these constraints, assemble Kubernetes and OS artifacts, validate them against NKE, and repeat that integration as upstream versions, security fixes, and NVIDIA components change. Upstream Kubernetes and existing distributions provide binaries, but they do not define the configuration contract NKE requires.

NKD moves that integration work into a reusable NVIDIA definition and a repeatable operator-run pipeline. The intended outcome is that an operator can build and start a compatible NKE deployment in days, then sustain it without rediscovering the integration for each release.

### 3.1 Customer

The primary customer is the AI Factory operator that provides self-service Kubernetes to internal business units or external tenants. Tenant self-service is exposed through NKE; tenants are not expected to build NKD artifacts.

### 3.2 Evidence and adoption hypothesis

DS9 is the first operator and MUST use the same released recipe, pipeline engine, supported builder profile, validation vector, and bootstrap path intended for external operators. NVIDIA MAY retain its canonical reference artifacts internally, but there MUST NOT be an internal-only definition, build implementation, or privileged input path.

Internal use validates the integration problem and exercises the system at scale. It does not, by itself, prove that external operators will accept an operator-run build pipeline. v1 adoption work MUST therefore validate both the problem and the delivery model with external design partners.

## 4\. Design decision {#4.-design-decision}

NKD v1 ships a distribution definition, the reproducible pipeline and supported builder profiles that materialize it, and the evidence required to verify the result. NVIDIA uses the same released contracts to build and validate canonical artifacts internally. It does not make those artifacts available for installation and does not host production OS images or package bundles for operators.

The ownership boundary is intentional:

> **NVIDIA owns** the definition, reproducible pipeline, supported builder profiles, canonical reference builds, and validation vectors. **The operator owns** its pipeline execution, reproduced or explicitly approved variant artifacts, promotion policy, and runtime environment.

This boundary does not eliminate NVIDIA's compatibility, security, or support obligations. Those obligations are made explicit in [Section 12](#bookmark=id.wfh51w56b7rq).

### 4.1 What withholding the reference bytes does and does not buy

Section 12 assigns NVIDIA recipe correctness, pipeline determinism, the compatibility matrix, lifecycle and advisories, security fixes, the conformance claim and suite, CVE policy, incident triage, and ValidatedVariant approval authority. That is substantially the full distributor obligation set. Withholding the bytes therefore cannot be justified as "avoiding distributor liability" in general, and this document does not make that claim. The specific and only obligations it avoids are:

- **Artifact hosting and egress** for production OS images and package bundles, at AI-Factory scale, in every operator geography and air-gap posture.\
- **A binary-artifact CVE-remediation SLA** distinct from the recipe-level SLA \- that is, an obligation to rebuild, re-host, and re-attest bytes on NVIDIA infrastructure for every operator on every advisory.\
- **A per-operator packaging and format matrix** \- registry layout, image format, kernel variant, and golden-image conventions that would otherwise become NVIDIA-supported product surface.

Everything else \- the definition, its validation, its security response, and its conformance evidence \- NVIDIA owns either way. The boundary is a **delivery and hosting decision, not a liability transfer.** Any argument for withholding that depends on a broader liability reduction is unsupported by Section 12 and MUST NOT be used in operator-facing material.

There is also a real cost to withholding, quantified in Section 8.4.2: the operator cannot diff against reference bytes, so the published reference content manifest must carry the diagnostic burden instead. The granularity of that manifest is the actual design dial, and it is a P0 open decision.

## 5\. Goals and non-goals {#5.-goals-and-non-goals}

### 5.1 Goals

NKD v1 MUST:

1. Define a complete, versioned configuration accepted by a declared range of NKE versions.\
2. Build and validate canonical reference artifacts inside NVIDIA using the exact recipe, pipeline, inputs, and supported builder profiles released to operators.\
3. Enable an operator to reproduce canonical OS images and Kubernetes packages with byte identities equal to NVIDIA's published reference identities for the selected supported builder profile.\
4. Publish a Kubernetes conformance claim for each released definition and enable an operator to validate that claim against a cluster instantiated from its own artifacts.\
5. Fail closed when inputs, artifacts, signatures, compatibility, reproducibility, or validation evidence do not match the selected recipe.\
6. Support repeatable bootstrap of the NKE Site Controller and subsequent NKE-managed workload clusters.\
7. Support image-based fleet upgrades with bounded workload interruption and a defined rollback path.\
8. Provide a time-bounded emergency security path without allowing permanent, untracked configuration drift.\
9. Expose sufficient evidence for an operator to audit what was defined, built, promoted, and deployed.\
10. Use AICR as the foundational declarative layer for the accelerated-runtime profile and its validated component pairings.\
11. Declare a bounded operator extension surface (Section 8.6) so that ordinary environment integration \- CA bundles, proxy, internal DNS/NTP, monitoring agents, authentication \- does not force an operator into fork status.\
12. Publish a builder-profile lifecycle and host re-baselining policy (Section 8.2.2) so that a third-party CI host image change does not become an unbounded operator outage.

### 5.2 Non-goals for v1

NKD v1 does not:

- publish a general-purpose Kubernetes distribution\
- distribute or host NVIDIA's canonical reference artifacts for operator installation\
- manage the operator's registry, secret store, build infrastructure, or artifact promotion\
- guarantee byte identity across undeclared host environments or compatibility for arbitrary operator modifications\
- claim that an operator-built cluster is conformant before the operator validates that instantiation\
- guarantee zero workload disruption during every node replacement\
- support arbitrary operating systems, architectures, Kubernetes versions, or NKE versions outside the published compatibility matrix\
- support more than **one** declared builder profile (Section 8.2.1); profile breadth is demand-driven after v1\
- offer QCOW2, VMDK, VHD, or any other container format as a byte-reproduced artifact; those are derived envelopes (Section 8.3.1)\
- support operator modifications outside the declared extension surface (Section 8.6)

Making reference artifacts downloadable MAY be introduced later as a convenience if external operators cannot or will not run the pipeline. They would not replace the definition or reproducible pipeline as the source of truth.

## 6\. Design principles and invariants {#6.-design-principles-and-invariants}

1. **Recipe before artifacts.** Every promoted artifact-set traces to exactly one immutable NKD distribution recipe\
2. **One released build implementation.** NVIDIA and operators MUST execute the same versioned pipeline engine and one declared supported builder profile; CI-specific workflows are adapters, not independent logic\
3. **Reference-first reproducibility.** NVIDIA builds first under each supported builder profile and publishes profile-specific canonical artifact digests. An operator build is Reproduced only when its selected profile and canonical payloads match\
4. **Operator-controlled supply chain.** Operator artifacts are built, stored, signed, and promoted under operator policy\
5. **Fail closed.** Missing provenance, incompatible versions, unverified inputs, or incomplete validation prevent promotion or deployment\
6. **Immutable normal path.** Normal changes produce a new image and replace nodes; running nodes are not patched in place\
7. **Explicit drift.** Emergency mutation is visible, expiring, and reconciled into a subsequent recipe\
8. **No privileged internal path.** Internal and external operators consume the same released interfaces\
9. **Identical contract, identical canonical output.** The recipe, pipeline, canonical inputs, and signed builder profile pin the complete reproducibility tuple. Byte identity is guaranteed only within that tuple. Operator-specific signatures and registry metadata are separate envelopes around the comparable payload\
10. **Evidence travels with the release.** A release includes the identities and evidence for NVIDIA's withheld reference artifacts: provenance, SBOMs, compatibility, conformance, and validation results\
11. **Controlled fallback.** A digest mismatch fails closed for the Reproduced state. Only a signed, time-bounded exception that passes all semantic, security, Kubernetes conformance, NKE integration, upgrade, and rollback gates can enter ValidatedVariant

## 7\. System architecture {#7.-system-architecture}

![][image1]\
The released product is the distribution recipe \+ pipeline engine \+ supported builder profiles \+ validation vectors. NVIDIA's reference artifacts stop at the release boundary. Operators select the same profile, import the recipe and engine through a thin CI adapter, and compare canonical delivery and content identities before promotion. Exact matches become Reproduced; only an explicitly approved fallback can become a separately identified ValidatedVariant.

### 7.1 Component responsibilities

| Component | Required responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| **NKD distribution recipe** | Declares the complete version, digest, configuration, compatibility, canonical inputs, and validation contract for one release. |
| **AICR** | Provides the foundational, declarative accelerated-runtime profile, including validated GPU and network operator pairings consumed by the NKD distribution recipe. |
| **Pipeline engine** | Materializes the recipe into canonical OS images and Kubernetes packages. It enforces the selected builder profile, performs preflight checks, and contains the authoritative build logic. |
| **CI adapters** | Invoke the exact pipeline engine from GitHub Actions, GitLab Pipelines, Jenkins, or another supported orchestrator. They MUST NOT reimplement build semantics or imply that CI brand alone defines reproducibility. |
| **NVIDIA reference pipeline** | Executes the released recipe and engine once for each supported builder profile, retains the outputs internally, and produces a profile-specific validation vector. |
| **Validation vector** | Publishes expected canonical digests, SBOMs, provenance, compatibility results, conformance evidence, and the comparison procedure without distributing the artifacts. |
| **Reproduction verifier** | Compares operator delivery and logical-content identities with the selected NVIDIA validation vector, emits stable mismatch diagnostics, and invokes variant review only for eligible causes. |
| **NKE** | Bootstraps and operates the Site Controller and workload clusters from a promoted, compatible artifact set. It does not build artifacts. |
| **NodeWright** | Replaces nodes under rollout and interruption policies; applies and reports the explicitly authorized emergency security path. |
| **NodeWrite and Package builder** | Implement image and package construction inside the pipeline engine. |
| **Operator systems** | Host a supported CI adapter and builder profile, mirror pinned inputs without changing content, execute the pipeline, add operator signatures, store and promote artifacts, and operate the runtime. |
| **Builder profile** | A signed, immutable declaration of the runner, kernel, architecture, filesystem, container runtime, virtualization, builder images, toolchains, Skysmith version, locale, clock, resource, and mirror prerequisites for one reference digest set. |

Component names describing the intended allocation from [NKD Product Proposal \+ Requirements Document](https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1gwnlSggRGriXN1Zl9rkHtExs2904HfGETtLqe4LEChI/edit) Concrete API ownership and integration maturity remain release-planning concerns.

### 7.2 AICR analogy

NKD applies the same separation AICR uses for runtime configuration at the Kubernetes distribution layer. AICR describes version-locked recipes, materializes them into deployer-specific bundles, and validates the running cluster. Its automation guidance keeps the underlying CLI operations constant across CI systems while changing only job syntax and artifact passing. NKD SHOULD preserve that separation.

| AICR concept | NKD analogue |
| :---- | :---- |
| Runtime recipe | Distribution recipe: Kubernetes, OS, core runtime, NKE, and AICR pairings |
| `aicr bundle` materializer | NKD pipeline engine that builds OS images and Kubernetes packages |
| Helm, Argo CD, Flux, or Helmfile bundle target | A signed builder profile plus a thin GitHub Actions, GitLab Pipelines, Jenkins, or other CI adapter. |
| `aicr validate` | Canonical artifact comparison plus runtime Kubernetes and NKE validation |
| Bundle provenance and evidence | NKD validation vector for NVIDIA's withheld reference artifacts |

References: [AICR overview](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aicr#readme) and [AICR automation model](https://github.com/NVIDIA/aicr/blob/main/docs/integrator/automation.md).

## 8\. Release contracts {#8.-release-contracts}

NKD needs machine-verifiable contracts between recipe publication, NVIDIA's reference build, operator reproduction, NKE bootstrap, and fleet rollout. File formats and schemas are open, but the following semantic content is required.

### 8.1 NKD distribution recipe

An immutable recipe MUST contain or reference by digest:

- a globally unique recipe identity and version;\
- compatible NKE versions\
- Kubernetes component versions and source or package digests\
- the AICR profile identity and digest\
- core and accelerated-runtime component versions and digests\
- the canonical base-image, operating-system, architecture, kernel, firmware, and driver inputs or constraints\
- required Kubernetes and NKE configuration\
- pipeline-engine and build-tool identities\
- one or more supported builder-profile identities and their profile-specific validation-vector references\
- normalized build parameters, artifact-specific canonicalization rules, and reproducibility policy\
- expected validation suites and policy thresholds\
- the Kubernetes conformance claim and validation-vector reference\
- known upgrade sources and targets\
- lifecycle state and support dates\
- NVIDIA signature and publication metadata

Publishing a recipe MUST be immutable. A correction produces a new identity; it does not mutate an existing release.

### 8.2 Pipeline bundle

The released pipeline bundle MUST contain or reference:

- the authoritative, hermetic build engine by immutable identity\
- stage definitions, interfaces, and failure semantics\
- pinned builder images, toolchains, locale, clock, archive, compression, filesystem, disk-image, and package normalization behavior\
- a canonical input resolver that fails on missing or mismatched content\
- a reproduction verifier independent of the artifact-producing stages\
- supported thin adapters for CI orchestrators\
- signed supported builder profiles and a fail-closed host-preflight implementation\
- an offline or mirrored execution path with equivalent verification behavior\
- the profile-specific deterministic diff tooling and reproduction evidence-bundle format

GitHub Actions, GitLab Pipelines, Jenkins, and other orchestrators are execution hosts. Their adapters MUST call the same pipeline engine and MUST NOT contain platform-specific artifact-construction logic. An orchestrator name is not a builder profile: different runners, kernels, filesystems, container runtimes, or virtualization capabilities under the same CI product can produce distinct profiles.

An operator MAY copy workflow definitions into its environment, but the copy MUST retain and verify the released pipeline-bundle identity. Local workflow changes that alter the engine invocation create a fork. Content-addressed import is preferred because an untracked copy will drift from NVIDIA's security and reproducibility updates.

### 8.2.1 Supported builder profile

Byte identity is guaranteed only for a complete supported builder profile that NVIDIA has used for a reference build. Each signed profile MUST identify:

- profile identity, version, lifecycle, and validation-vector identity\
- CI orchestrator and adapter versions, while keeping build semantics in the engine\
- runner OS, kernel, architecture, CPU features, filesystem and mount behavior\
- container runtime, storage driver, virtualization or KVM capabilities, and resource minima\
- builder-image, pipeline-engine, Skysmith, package-builder, and toolchain digests\
- locale, time zone, umask, clock or SOURCE\_DATE\_EPOCH, network, mirror, and egress policy

The engine MUST run profile preflight before resolving build inputs and MUST stop when a required host property is absent or differs. NVIDIA MUST publish one reference build and digest vector for every supported profile. Same input content executed outside a supported profile is experimental and cannot claim byte reproduction, even when the CI brand is nominally supported.\
The profile SHOULD minimize host dependence by placing construction in pinned builder images. Host properties that cannot be isolated-such as kernel, filesystem, virtualization, or block-device behavior-remain explicit profile fields and conformance-test inputs.

**A profile identifier is a label, not the identity.** An identifier such as `gha-ubuntu-24.04-amd64-v1` names only the orchestrator, runner image, and architecture; it does not encode kernel, container runtime, filesystem, or virtualization, which are equally determinative. The signed profile digest is the authoritative identity, and all comparison, preflight, and telemetry MUST key on the digest.

#### v1 profile scope

**NKD v1 declares exactly one supported builder profile.** Every additional profile multiplies a fixed, non-amortizable cost: one NVIDIA reference build, one signed validation vector, and one full pass of the Section 14.2 validation suite \- conformance, NKE integration, bootstrap, upgrade, rollback, GPU and high-performance-network operation, and failure injection \- repeated per release. Because a profile is the cross product of orchestrator, runner OS, kernel, architecture, filesystem, container runtime, and virtualization, an uncapped profile set makes Phase 0 unbounded and the per-release validation cost unpredictable.

Profile breadth is therefore demand-driven after v1. Each candidate profile MUST be justified by design-partner demand and MUST carry a published incremental validation cost before it is added. Operators whose environment does not match the v1 profile use a self-hosted runner conforming to it; that is a supported path and is the intended answer during v1.

### 8.2.2 Builder-profile lifecycle and host re-baselining

A supported builder profile pins host properties \- runner kernel, filesystem behavior, container runtime, virtualization \- that NVIDIA does not control and the operator does not control. Hosted CI providers rotate runner images on their own cadence, without notice and without operator opt-out. Because preflight fails closed (Section 13), an upstream runner-image rotation would otherwise halt **every operator on that profile simultaneously**, with no operator-side remedy, until NVIDIA republished a profile, a reference build, and a digest vector.

NKD v1 MUST bound that exposure:

- Every supported profile MUST declare a **host-control class**: `operator-controlled` (self-hosted or pinned runner image the operator holds) or `provider-controlled` (a hosted runner image the CI provider rotates).\
- At least one `operator-controlled` profile MUST exist for every released recipe, so that no release is reachable only through infrastructure NVIDIA and the operator both lack control over.\
- Each profile MUST declare which fields are **hard-fail** at preflight and which are **advisory**. A field MUST NOT be hard-fail unless a divergence in it has been demonstrated to change canonical output. Fields not demonstrated to affect output are recorded in the evidence bundle and reported, but do not stop the build.\
- NVIDIA MUST publish a **re-baseline SLA**: the maximum time from a detected provider host change to a republished profile, reference build, and validation vector for `provider-controlled` profiles.\
- During re-baselining, the superseded profile and its vector MUST remain valid for a declared **grace window** so that in-flight operator builds and rebuilds of an existing release remain reproducible.\
- Profile deprecation MUST publish a successor profile and an overlap window. A profile MUST NOT be withdrawn while a supported recipe references it as its only profile.

The commercial terms of the re-baseline SLA and grace window are a P0 open decision (Section 19).

### 8.3 Build inputs and byte-identity boundary

Every input capable of changing canonical output MUST be pinned and recorded, including:

- base-image and source digests\
- package-repository snapshot identity and package digests\
- selected supported builder-profile identity and builder-image digests\
- toolchain and pipeline-engine identity\
- normalized environment values\
- the NKD recipe and AICR profile identities

Operator-specific values such as registry location, mutable tags, credentials, signing keys, attestation timestamps, and promotion metadata MUST NOT change the canonical payload being compared. They are applied as a separate envelope after successful reproduction. Secrets MUST be referenced, not embedded in artifacts, manifests, or logs.

An operator change to a canonical input or supported builder profile produces a variant, not a reproduction. A later runtime conformance pass cannot convert it into Reproduced; it can contribute only to the separately gated ValidatedVariant decision.

### 8.3.1 Artifact-specific canonicalization

The recipe MUST declare both the logical content boundary and the delivery-byte boundary for each artifact.

**RAW is the canonical OS-image artifact.** It is the only disk format whose byte boundary is unambiguous \- a digest over the logical LBA stream, with no container header, no allocation metadata, and no writer-tool version embedded in the payload. Every other disk format is a **derived delivery envelope**: a deterministic conversion of the reproduced RAW image, verified by logical-disk digest, never by container-file digest.

This is a deliberate change from treating QCOW2 as a byte-reproduced artifact. QCOW2 embeds writer-tool version, header padding, image UUID, refcount ordering, cluster size, and compression state \- all of which vary across otherwise identical hosts. Making it a canonical delivery artifact would route the flagship OS artifact into VariantReview as a matter of routine, which is precisely the erosion risk recorded in Section 18\. Converting after reproduction removes that class of exception entirely.

| Format | Role | Comparable boundary | Required normalization and exclusions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| OCI image or bundle | canonical | OCI manifest, config, and layer digests referenced by the release manifest. | Pin media types and compression. Tags, registry URLs, signatures, referrers, and registry metadata are outside the canonical payload. |
| DEB, RPM, tar, or package bundle | canonical | Exact unsigned package or archive bytes plus per-entry content manifest. | Normalize timestamps, uid/gid, mode, ordering, compressor and packaging-tool versions. Operator signatures are outside the boundary. |
| **RAW disk image** | **canonical** | SHA-256 over the complete logical LBA stream \[0, virtual\_size); sparse holes are read as zero bytes. | Includes partition table, bootloader, filesystem UUIDs, and file content. Host sparse allocation and host file metadata are excluded. |
| QCOW2, VMDK, VHD | derived envelope | Logical-disk digest of the decoded block stream MUST equal the reproduced RAW digest. The container file itself is **not** compared. | Conversion MUST be a declared, pinned, deterministic step in the recipe. Writer-tool version, header fields, image UUID, refcounts, cluster size, and compression are outside the boundary by construction. |
| ISO | canonical | Exact unsigned ISO bytes plus a content-tree manifest. | Normalize volume identifier, timestamps, directory order, boot catalog identifiers, and ISO tool version. |

Envelope conversion happens **after** the Reproduced state is established, alongside operator signing and registry metadata (Section 8.3). A conversion-step mismatch is a tooling defect in a declared pinned step, not a reproduction failure, and MUST NOT enter VariantReview: the operator re-runs the conversion from the already-reproduced RAW image.

The recipe MUST deterministically set partition identifiers, filesystem UUIDs, machine-id behavior, and default cloud-init content. A field that is intentionally operator-specific MUST be outside both the canonical image and its content manifest or must be represented as an explicitly declared post-reproduction envelope.

### 8.4 Artifact release set and validation vector

Both NVIDIA and operator builds MUST produce one atomic release set containing:

- canonical bootable OS image or images for the declared platform\
- matching canonical Kubernetes package bundle\
- a release manifest linking every canonical artifact digest to the recipe, pipeline, and complete input manifest\
- per-artifact and aggregate SBOMs\
- build provenance\
- compatibility and validation results\
- documented bootstrap inputs

NVIDIA retains its reference release sets internally. For each supported builder profile it publishes a signed validation vector containing delivery and logical-content digests, release manifest, SBOMs, provenance, conformance results, comparison rules, and enough normalized metadata to explain a mismatch without exposing artifact bytes.

The operator MUST compare its canonical payloads with the vector for its selected builder profile before adding its own signatures and promotion metadata. NKE and NodeWright MUST select operator release sets by immutable identity or digest, never by mutable tag alone. Promotion MUST be atomic: partial sets are not deployable; mismatched sets require an approved ValidatedVariant exception and distinct identity.

### 8.4.1 ValidatedVariant fallback

Digest mismatch fails closed for Reproduced. A release set MAY enter VariantReview only when the mismatch is caused by a documented representation or host nondeterminism that cannot be eliminated in the selected supported builder profile.

Approval requires all of the following:

- the selected builder profile is supported and its preflight, input manifest, and provenance are complete\
- the cause is classified as NONDETERMINISTIC\_METADATA or another explicitly permitted representation difference-not component, package, configuration, or unknown drift\
- logical content manifests and format-specific semantic comparisons match\
- SBOM, vulnerability, integrity, and policy checks pass\
- the full Kubernetes conformance, NKE integration, bootstrap, upgrade, and rollback suites pass\
- an authorized NVIDIA approver signs an exception identifier, rationale, exact artifact identities, support scope, and expiry

An approved output receives a distinct ValidatedVariant identity and validation vector. It MUST NOT be described as byte-reproduced NKD, MUST NOT reuse the reference artifact identity, and MUST be rebuilt or reapproved at expiry. CONTENT\_MISMATCH, INPUT\_MISMATCH, TOOLCHAIN\_DEFECT, and UNKNOWN are ineligible until corrected or reclassified with evidence.

**Pre-classified causes and the self-service requirement.** Requiring a human NVIDIA signature for every mismatch would contradict the product P0 in Section 17: an operator that hits any representation difference could not complete without contacting NVIDIA. Approval is therefore two-tier:

| Tier | Cause | Approval |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Pre-classified** | A cause NVIDIA has already characterized for this recipe and profile, enumerated by identifier in the validation vector, with its permitted divergence expressed as a machine-checkable predicate. | Automatic, on the operator's own infrastructure, when the predicate holds and every gate above passes. Recorded and reported; no NVIDIA round trip. |
| **Novel** | Any eligible representation cause not already enumerated. | Signed NVIDIA exception, as above. |

Each novel cause that survives review MUST be evaluated for promotion to pre-classified in the next release of the affected recipe, so repeat occurrences stop generating support contacts. A pre-classified approval carries the same ValidatedVariant identity semantics, expiry, and support scope as a signed one, and is equally excluded from the byte-reproduced claim. The set of pre-classified causes MUST be published in the validation vector, never inferred by the operator.

### 8.4.2 Reference content-manifest granularity

Because NVIDIA withholds the reference bytes, the operator cannot diff against them. The published reference content manifest carries the entire diagnostic burden instead, and its **granularity is the design dial** that determines whether Section 13.1 triage is executable:

- Too coarse \- a single digest per artifact \- and a mismatch is detectable but not explainable. The operator learns only that byte 0 through the end differ somewhere. Section 18 records this as a live risk.\
- Fine enough to locate a divergence \- per-block hashes over the RAW LBA stream and a per-path filesystem manifest \- and the manifest approaches a Merkle tree over the image. It reveals structure and content identity, though not the bytes themselves.

The v1 requirement is that granularity MUST be sufficient to satisfy Section 13.1 step 4 without access to reference bytes. Concretely, each validation vector MUST publish:

- a per-artifact aggregate digest,\
- for disk images, block-range digests over the canonical RAW LBA stream at a declared fixed block size,\
- a per-path content manifest (path, mode, uid/gid, size, content digest) for every filesystem in the image,\
- a per-entry manifest for package bundles and archives,\
- normalized build metadata sufficient to distinguish a host-representation cause from a content cause.

The declared block size, manifest schema, and any deliberate redaction MUST be published with the vector, because they bound what an operator can diagnose alone. Selecting that granularity \- and confirming that the resulting disclosure is acceptable given that withholding bytes buys only what Section 4.1 enumerates \- is a P0 open decision.

### 8.5 NKE consumption contract

Before bootstrap or upgrade, NKE MUST verify:

1. recipe, pipeline, selected builder-profile, input-manifest, validation-vector, and artifact identities\
2. either a successful exact comparison with the selected NVIDIA validation vector or a current, signed ValidatedVariant exception\
3. operator signatures and provenance under operator trust policy\
4. release-set completeness\
5. NKE, Kubernetes, OS, architecture, and accelerated-stack compatibility\
6. the required predeployment validation results or an operator-approved exception where policy permits one

An unsupported, incomplete, or non-identical release set without a current ValidatedVariant exception MUST be rejected before infrastructure is mutated. Runtime conformance and NKE validation then gate Active status and production promotion; they cannot be completed through static inspection.

### 8.6 Operator extension surface

Section 12 classifies every operator change as a published tuple, a variant, or a fork, and references "supported overlays" and "declared extension points." Neither is defined elsewhere in this document. Without a definition, ordinary environment integration \- the corporate CA bundle, an outbound proxy, internal DNS and NTP, an EDR or monitoring agent, site authentication \- has only two outcomes: silently break byte reproduction, or make the operator a fork and lose support. Every real operator needs at least one of these on day one. This is the most likely cause of v1 adoption failure, and it is a design obligation, not something to be measured in Phase 2\.

NKD v1 MUST declare a bounded extension surface with three tiers:

| Tier | Definition | Effect on reproduction | Support |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Envelope extension** | Applied after the Reproduced state, outside the canonical payload: registry metadata, operator signatures, delivery-format conversion (Section 8.3.1). | None. Canonical payload is unchanged and still matches the vector. | Full |
| **Declared overlay** | A named, schema-constrained modification the recipe explicitly permits, applied at first boot or as a declared post-reproduction layer \- trust anchors, proxy and network configuration, resolver and time sources, an approved agent set, authentication and authorization config. | None on the canonical artifact. The overlay is a separate, digested, operator-owned object recorded in the release-set identity. | Full for NKD and NKE; overlay content is operator-owned |
| **Fork** | Anything else: a changed canonical input, a modified pipeline stage, an unsupported builder profile, or an image mutation outside the declared overlay schema. | Byte identity is void. | Not covered unless separately qualified |

Requirements:

- The recipe MUST declare the overlay schema: which configuration domains are extensible, their constraints, and their application point.\
- An overlay MUST NOT be able to alter Kubernetes, kubelet, container-runtime, or accelerated-stack versions or configuration that the conformance and NKE-compatibility claims depend on. Anything that can is a fork by construction.\
- Overlays MUST be digested and carried in the release-set identity and in node-reported state, so a node running an overlay is distinguishable from one that is not, without being marked drifted (Section 10.3).\
- Applying a declared overlay MUST NOT change the Reproduced status of the canonical artifacts it is layered onto.\
- The operator MUST run the conformance and NKE validation suites against the overlaid instantiation, not the bare one, because the overlay is part of what runs.

An operator need that cannot be met within the overlay schema is signal to extend the schema in a subsequent recipe, not to expand fork tolerance. The initial overlay domain list is a P0 open decision.

## 9\. End-to-end lifecycle {#9.-end-to-end-lifecycle}

### 9.1 NVIDIA reference build and publication

1. NVIDIA selects and pins upstream and NVIDIA component inputs; AICR supplies the validated accelerated-runtime profile\
2. NVIDIA freezes a recipe, pipeline bundle, complete canonical input manifest, and supported builder profiles\
3. NVIDIA runs the released pipeline engine once under each supported builder profile and builds a canonical reference release set per profile\
4. Independent verification records artifact digests, SBOMs, provenance, compatibility, security results, and reproducibility metadata\
5. NVIDIA instantiates the reference artifacts and runs Kubernetes conformance, NKE, upgrade, rollback, and operational validation\
6. NVIDIA retains the reference artifacts internally and signs and publishes only the recipe, pipeline bundle, validation vector, conformance claim, and lifecycle metadata

### 9.2 Operator reproduction and promotion

1. The operator selects a supported NKD release and one of its signed builder profiles, then verifies both\
2. It copies or imports the pipeline bundle into a supported CI orchestrator, satisfies builder-profile preflight, and mirrors the exact pinned inputs without changing their content\
3. A thin CI adapter invokes the released pipeline engine\
4. The engine creates the operator's canonical release set; a separate verifier compares every canonical payload with NVIDIA's validation vector\
5. Any mismatch fails closed for Reproduced with artifact- and content-level diagnostics. The operator corrects the cause or, for an eligible representation difference, requests the separately gated ValidatedVariant review; runtime conformance alone cannot convert a mismatch into reproduction.\
6. After a successful exact match-or after receipt of a current signed ValidatedVariant exception-the operator adds its signatures and provenance envelope and promotes the distinctly identified release set to a candidate registry\
7. The operator instantiates a test cluster, runs the released conformance and NKE validation suites, and promotes the release for production use only after they pass

Any failed or interrupted stage leaves an unpromoted candidate. Re-running with the same complete canonical input set under the same supported builder profile MUST reproduce the profile-specific NVIDIA artifact identities.

### 9.3 Bootstrap and cluster provisioning

1. The operator selects a candidate or production release set that either matched its profile-specific validation vector or carries a current signed ValidatedVariant exception\
2. NKE verifies the consumption contract before bootstrap\
3. The operator boots Site Controller machines from the promoted image\
4. NKE installs the matching Kubernetes packages and management controllers\
5. NKE validates Site Controller readiness\
6. Operators or tenants request workload clusters through the NKE API\
7. NKE provisions each cluster from a compatible promoted release set and reports its effective recipe and artifact identities

Readiness MUST include control-plane health and the configured DNS, storage, networking, policy, telemetry, GPU, and high-performance network checks. Node registration alone is not sufficient.

### 9.4 Normal upgrade

1. NVIDIA publishes a new recipe and validation vector with supported upgrade edges\
2. The operator builds, validates, and promotes a new release set\
3. NKE verifies compatibility and requests a rollout\
4. NodeWright replaces nodes under configured capacity, health, and interruption budgets\
5. The rollout pauses on failed health gates or an exhausted budget\
6. The fleet is complete only when all targeted nodes report the new recipe and artifact identities and no unauthorized drift remains

The system MUST NOT claim that replacement is disruption-free. Long-running jobs, stateful workloads, failed drains, and unavailable spare capacity can delay or interrupt an upgrade. Those conditions MUST be surfaced before or during rollout.

### 9.5 Emergency security path

An in-place security fix is an explicit exception to the immutable normal path:

1. NVIDIA publishes an advisory identifying affected recipes, the approved mutation, validation evidence, and a reconciliation deadline\
2. The operator explicitly authorizes the emergency action\
3. NodeWright applies the fix and records affected nodes, before-and-after state, time, and result\
4. Nodes enter the `EmergencyDrift` state and remain visible as non-converged\
5. NVIDIA incorporates the fix into a new recipe and reference build\
6. The operator rebuilds and replaces affected nodes before the deadline

Emergency drift MUST be detectable, time-bounded, and prevented from silently becoming the fleet baseline. An operator that applies the exact NVIDIA-authorized fix, retains required evidence, and reconciles before the advisory deadline remains within the normal NKE support SLA. Missing the deadline or introducing out-of-scope changes moves affected nodes to UnsupportedDrift: drift-related support becomes best-effort until reconciliation, while unrelated incidents remain subject to the base support contract. Exact commercial SLA and liability terms remain governed by the published product support policy.

### 9.6 Release cadence

Because the operator runs the pipeline, NVIDIA's release frequency is directly an operator cost: every published recipe obliges the operator to rebuild, re-verify reproduction, re-run conformance and NKE validation, promote, and roll the fleet. A distribution vendor absorbs that cost centrally; NKD distributes it. Operators will size CI capacity, staffing, and change windows on this number, and they will ask for it during evaluation.

NKD v1 MUST therefore publish an expected steady-state cadence for each release class, not only a per-release notice:

| Class | Trigger | Operator obligation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Scheduled | Kubernetes patch, base-image refresh, AICR pairing update | Rebuild and roll within the declared support window |
| Security | CVE meeting the published severity threshold | Rebuild on the advisory timeline, or use the Section 9.5 emergency path and reconcile before its deadline |
| Corrective | Recipe or pipeline defect | Rebuild only if the operator is affected, per the advisory |

Every input pinned by digest is a potential trigger: a CVE anywhere in the base image, kernel, or package snapshot invalidates the reference build and requires a new reference build per supported profile before any operator can converge. Cadence, the batching policy that keeps it tractable, and the maximum interval an operator may remain on a superseded recipe while supported are P0 open decisions.

## 10\. Reproducibility, immutability, and drift {#10.-reproducibility,-immutability,-and-drift}

### 10.1 Canonical byte-identity guarantee

Byte-for-byte reproduction of canonical artifacts is an NKD v1 requirement within a published supported builder profile. It is not a cross-profile guarantee. The reproducibility tuple is:

```
NKD recipe digest
+ pipeline-engine digest
+ canonical input-manifest digest
+ supported builder-profile digest
= canonical artifact digest set
```

NVIDIA and an operator using the same tuple MUST produce identical bytes for every artifact the recipe marks **canonical**, at the boundary Section 8.3.1 declares for that artifact's format. The MUST attaches to the canonical boundary, not to every file the pipeline emits: derived delivery envelopes such as QCOW2, VMDK, and VHD are verified by logical-disk digest against the reproduced RAW image and are explicitly outside this guarantee. NVIDIA publishes the expected digest set separately for each supported builder profile; the operator proves reproduction by selecting that profile, passing preflight, and matching its vector.

This guarantee requires the pipeline to normalize or pin every source of variability, including base-image bytes, repository snapshots, timestamps, locale, filesystem and archive ordering, ownership metadata, compression, toolchains, builder images, runner kernel, filesystem behavior, container runtime, virtualization, and available resources. A customer-supplied base image or host property that differs from the selected profile produces a variant and cannot claim byte identity with NVIDIA's reference build.

Operator-specific values are intentionally outside the comparison boundary:

- registry host and mutable tags\
- credentials and secrets\
- operator signing keys and signatures\
- attestation and promotion timestamps\
- environment-specific deployment metadata

The pipeline MUST compare canonical unsigned payloads before applying this operator envelope. If a packaging format cannot separate these values, its content-level digest boundary and deterministic encoding MUST be specified explicitly.

### 10.2 Two independent validation vectors

Reproducibility and Kubernetes conformance answer different questions:

| Proof | Question answered | Required evidence |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Artifact reproduction | Did the operator produce the same bytes NVIDIA built and validated? | Exact delivery and logical-content digest match against the signed validation vector for the selected supported builder profile. |
| Runtime conformance | Does the operator's instantiated cluster behave as claimed? | The released Kubernetes conformance and NKE validation suites run against that cluster |

Passing conformance cannot make an artifact Reproduced, and matching artifact bytes does not prove the deployed cluster is correctly configured. Both gates are required for ordinary promotion. A conformance pass may contribute to ValidatedVariant only after the mismatch is eligible, logical equivalence is proven, all additional gates pass, and NVIDIA signs the exception.

The reproduction verifier SHOULD be independently implemented or, at minimum, isolated from the build stages so a pipeline defect cannot manufacture both an artifact and its proof. Because NVIDIA withholds the reference bytes, every profile-specific validation vector MUST publish enough signed evidence to diagnose divergence: aggregate, delivery, logical-content, and component digests; content manifests; SBOMs; provenance; normalized build metadata; and stable mismatch codes.

### 10.3 Runtime invariants

- Every node MUST report the recipe and artifact release-set identities it runs.\
- A node is conformant only when its observed state matches the promoted release set or an active, authorized emergency advisory.\
- Unrecognized mutation MUST mark the node drifted and block a healthy-convergence claim.\
- Normal remediation replaces the node from a promoted release set.

## 11\. Security and trust model {#11.-security-and-trust-model}

### 11.1 Trust boundaries

| Boundary | Required control |
| :---- | :---- |
| NVIDIA reference build | Isolated execution of the released engine; complete input capture; independent artifact and runtime validation. |
| NVIDIA publication | Signed, immutable recipe, pipeline bundle, validation vector, lifecycle metadata, and auditable release identity. |
| Dependency resolution | Digest pinning, signature or provenance verification, mirror policy, and fail-closed resolution. |
| CI adapter | Minimal orchestration only; immutable engine invocation; no platform-specific build logic. |
| Operator build | Isolated and least-privileged execution; supported builder-profile preflight; exact canonical inputs; secret redaction; recorded input, host, and builder identity. |
| Reproduction check | Independent comparison of canonical payloads before operator signing or promotion. |
| Candidate promotion | Policy evaluation, malware and vulnerability scans, SBOM and provenance verification, and operator signature. |
| NKE deployment | Immutable identity selection, trust-policy verification, compatibility check, and admission audit. |
| Node operation | Attested or observed release identity, drift detection, bounded credentials, and emergency-change audit. |

### 11.2 Required security properties

- Recipes, pipeline bundles, validation vectors, and operator release sets MUST be integrity protected and independently addressable by digest\
- Expected artifact digests MUST be authenticated by the signed validation vector; an unauthenticated digest is not a trusted reference\
- The NVIDIA reference pipeline MUST use the same released engine and canonical inputs available to operators\
- The pipeline MUST NOT emit credentials into artifacts, SBOMs, provenance, or logs\
- Vulnerability results and exceptions MUST identify the scanned artifact and policy version\
- Security updates MUST identify affected recipe versions and supported remediation paths\
- Compromise of an operator registry MUST NOT allow an untrusted mutable tag to bypass digest and signature verification\
- Air-gapped operation MUST preserve the same verification semantics as connected operation; the transport mechanism is open

## 12\. Support and responsibility boundary {#12.-support-and-responsibility-boundary}

Owning the generated artifacts does not make the operator solely responsible for defects in the NVIDIA recipe or pipeline. The proposed v1 boundary is:

| Area | NVIDIA responsibility | Operator responsibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Recipe | Correctness, signatures, compatibility matrix, lifecycle, advisories, and documented upgrade edges. | Select a supported recipe and do not alter it while claiming reproduction. |
| Pipeline engine | Deterministic behavior within each supported builder profile; profile lifecycle; release notes; security fixes; CI-neutral interfaces; preflight; and diagnostics. | Execute the released engine from a supported adapter under a supported builder profile and preserve logs and evidence. |
| Canonical inputs | Publish immutable identities, mirror requirements, and availability rules. | Mirror and provide the exact content without substitution. |
| Reference artifacts | Build, retain, validate, and publish their signed validation vector; do not distribute the bytes. | Reproduce the bytes and compare them with the vector. |
| Operator artifacts | Define canonical content and comparison rules. | Apply operator signatures, scan, promote, retain, and protect reproduced artifacts. |
| Reproducibility | Normalize variable inputs, publish profile-specific identities, and support deterministic mismatch diagnosis. | Fail promotion as Reproduced on mismatch, follow the diagnostic workflow, and disclose any input, profile, or engine deviation during support. |
| NKE integration | Support NKE against conformant release sets. | Deploy compatible NKE and release-set versions. |
| Fleet operations | Provide rollout behavior, health signals, and supported remediation. | Set capacity and interruption budgets; operate workloads and infrastructure. |
| Incident response | Triage recipe, pipeline, and NKE defects and publish applicable remediation. | Triage environment-specific failures and provide reproducible evidence. |
| Conformance | Publish the Kubernetes conformance claim, reference evidence, exact suite, and validation tooling for each recipe. | Run the suite against the operator-built instantiation and retain results linked to its release set. |
| ValidatedVariant | Approve only eligible representation differences after all required gates; publish signed scope, identity, support status, and expiry. | Do not claim byte reproduction; retain exception evidence; operate only within its scope; rebuild or reapprove before expiry. |
| EmergencyDrift | Publish affected recipes, authorized mutation, evidence requirements, support scope, and reconciliation deadline. | Apply only the authorized change, retain evidence, and reconcile before the deadline. Missed deadlines or out-of-scope changes enter UnsupportedDrift. |
| Builder-profile lifecycle | Maintain at least one operator-controlled profile per recipe; publish the re-baseline SLA, grace window, and successor profile on deprecation (Section 8.2.2). | Track profile lifecycle notices; migrate to a successor profile within the overlap window. |
| Extension surface | Declare and version the overlay schema; keep it sufficient for ordinary environment integration (Section 8.6). | Confine modifications to the declared surface; digest and report overlays; validate the overlaid instantiation. |
| Release cadence | Publish expected cadence per release class and the maximum supported interval on a superseded recipe (Section 9.6). | Size build and rollout capacity to the published cadence; converge within the declared window. |

Operator changes MUST be classified, using the extension surface defined in Section 8.6:

- **Published tuple:** an allowed parameter and builder-profile selection that resolves to its own signed recipe, input manifest, validation vector, and expected artifact digest set; eligible for reproduction\
- **Envelope extension or declared overlay:** a change confined to the Section 8.6 extension surface; does not affect the canonical payload and remains eligible for reproduction and full support\
- **Variant:** a changed canonical input, an unsupported builder profile, or an overlay outside the declared schema; may enter review but cannot claim byte identity\
- **Fork:** changed pipeline semantics or inputs outside declared extension points; not covered unless NVIDIA separately qualifies it

The final commercial support and incident-liability policy is a release blocker and must be consistent with this technical boundary.

## 13\. Failure handling and recovery {#13.-failure-handling-and-recovery}

| Failure | Required behavior | Recovery |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Recipe or pipeline signature failure | Stop before build. | Refresh trusted metadata or select a trusted release. |
| Unavailable or digest-mismatched input | Stop; do not substitute a newer artifact. | Restore the pinned input or select a newer recipe. |
| Builder-profile preflight mismatch, hard-fail field | Stop before input resolution or build; report every unsatisfied profile field. | Use a runner matching the selected profile or select another published profile and its vector. |
| Builder-profile preflight mismatch, advisory field | Record in the evidence bundle and continue; do not stop the build. | None required; the divergence is reported with the reproduction result. |
| Provider-controlled host image changed under a supported profile | Report `BUILDER_PROFILE_MISMATCH` identifying the changed host property and the affected profile. | Use the operator-controlled profile for the same recipe, or wait for the republished profile within the declared re-baseline SLA; the superseded profile and vector stay valid through the grace window (Section 8.2.2). |
| Delivery-envelope conversion mismatch | Report a conversion-step defect against the pinned tool; do not alter the Reproduced state of the canonical RAW artifact. | Re-run the declared conversion from the reproduced RAW image. MUST NOT enter VariantReview. |
| Operator modification outside the declared overlay schema | Classify as fork before build; do not compare against the validation vector. | Move the change inside the Section 8.6 overlay schema, or request the schema be extended in a subsequent recipe. |
| Partial build | Keep candidate unpromoted and clearly incomplete. | Resume safely or rebuild from recorded inputs. |
| Canonical artifact digest mismatch | Block the Reproduced state and emit delivery-, component-, and logical-content diagnostics. | Follow Section 13.1, correct and rebuild, or request VariantReview only for an eligible representation difference. |
| Validation vector unavailable or unauthenticated | Stop reproduction verification; do not trust cached mutable metadata. | Restore a signed vector through the release or offline channel. |
| Validation or policy failure | Reject promotion and retain diagnostics. | Fix operator input or consume a corrected recipe or pipeline release. |
| Bootstrap incompatibility | Reject before machine mutation where possible. | Select a compatible NKE and release set. |
| Bootstrap readiness failure | Report failed gate and preserve evidence. | Retry idempotently or restore the previously promoted Site Controller release under a documented procedure. |
| Node drain or replacement failure | Pause within the interruption budget; do not declare convergence. | Resolve workload/capacity constraints, retry, or roll back to a supported release set. |
| Post-upgrade health regression | Halt further rollout. | Replace affected nodes from the prior supported release set when downgrade compatibility permits. |
| Emergency fix failure or expiry | Mark affected nodes non-converged and alert. | Retry approved remediation or replace nodes from a reconciled release. |
| CI adapter invokes a different engine or changes build semantics | Stop before build and identify the unsupported adapter behavior. | Restore the released adapter and engine identities. |
| ValidatedVariant exception expires | Block new deployment and mark existing use exception-expired; do not relabel it Reproduced. | Rebuild to exact identity, replace with a supported release, or obtain a new approval after rerunning all gates. |
| EmergencyDrift deadline missed | Move affected nodes to UnsupportedDrift and alert; apply drift-related best-effort support until reconciliation. | Replace or reconcile affected nodes from a current supported recipe and restore Active only after validation. |

Retries MUST be bounded and observable. Recovery MUST preserve the last known-good release identity and evidence. Control-plane and data compatibility rules for rollback must be encoded in the recipe rather than inferred during an incident.

**Section 13.1 is the normative source for mismatch classification.** The cause codes, their eligibility for VariantReview, and the triage order are defined there and referenced \- not restated \- by Section 8.4.1, this table, and Section 18\. A change to the taxonomy is a change to Section 13.1 only.

### 13.1 Digest mismatch triage

The verifier MUST generate a signed reproduction evidence bundle and execute this deterministic workflow:

1. Verify the recipe, pipeline, selected builder profile, canonical input manifest, validation vector, and signatures. Stop if any identity differs\
2. Rerun builder-profile preflight and record expected and observed runner, kernel, filesystem, container-runtime, virtualization, toolchain, clock, and resource properties.\
3. Compare aggregate release-set and per-artifact delivery digests; identify the first divergent artifact without treating order as root cause.\
4. Run the format-specific diff: compare OCI manifest/config/layers; package metadata and payload manifests; disk block-range hashes followed by a read-only filesystem manifest; or ISO content trees.\
5. Classify the cause as INPUT\_MISMATCH, BUILDER\_PROFILE\_MISMATCH, NONDETERMINISTIC\_METADATA, CONTENT\_MISMATCH, TOOLCHAIN\_DEFECT, or UNKNOWN. Include artifact, path or block range, expected/actual identity, and stage.\
6. Correct the cause and rebuild. After two identical unexplained failures, escalate with the complete evidence bundle rather than repeatedly retrying.\
7. Permit VariantReview only for an explicitly eligible representation difference. CONTENT\_MISMATCH, INPUT\_MISMATCH, TOOLCHAIN\_DEFECT, and UNKNOWN remain blocked until corrected or reclassified with evidence.

The evidence bundle MUST contain the profile-preflight report, normalized environment, complete input manifest, stage logs, delivery and logical-content manifests, mismatch code, diff output, SBOM, provenance, and trace identifiers. It MUST NOT contain credentials or operator signing keys.

## 14\. Validation and conformance {#14.-validation-and-conformance}

### 14.1 NKD Kubernetes conformance claim

Each released NKD recipe MUST carry a Kubernetes conformance claim. The claim MUST identify:

- the exact NKD recipe and Kubernetes version\
- the conformance suite, version, configuration, and pass criteria\
- the NVIDIA reference environment and artifact release set tested\
- the complete results and any permitted exclusions\
- the process an operator uses to validate the claim for its own instantiation

The claim applies to the released NKD recipe and the declared supported input constraints. It is substantiated first by NVIDIA's reference results and then, for an operator-built cluster, by that operator running the same conformance validation against the deployed cluster. Static inspection of the built artifacts alone is insufficient because Kubernetes conformance is a property of the running cluster.

### 14.2 NVIDIA release validation

Before publication, NVIDIA MUST build canonical reference artifacts with the released pipeline and validate those exact artifacts against representative supported environments and declared NKE versions.

The suite MUST cover at least:

- canonical digest reproduction across independent NVIDIA executions of every supported builder profile\
- artifact and provenance verification\
- bootstrap and repeat bootstrap\
- the declared Kubernetes conformance suite\
- Kubernetes control-plane and node health\
- NKE management controllers\
- networking, DNS, storage, and policy prerequisites\
- GPU and high-performance network discovery and operation\
- upgrade and rollback edges\
- interruption-budget behavior\
- failure injection for unavailable, corrupt, and incompatible inputs\
- emergency security reconciliation

The evidence MUST identify the exact recipe, pipeline, builder profile, input manifest, canonical artifact digests, tools, environment, and result. NVIDIA retains the validated artifact bytes and publishes their signed profile-specific validation vector. NVIDIA's result substantiates the NKD recipe's technical claim; it does not prove that an independently built operator cluster passed until that cluster is tested.

### 14.3 Operator artifact reproduction

The operator MUST build with the released recipe, pipeline engine, canonical inputs, and a supported builder profile, then compare every canonical payload with that profile's signed validation vector. Exact delivery and logical-content identity is the primary Reproduced pass criterion. Component and content manifests provide mismatch diagnostics; they do not weaken that state.

The operator does not need access to NVIDIA's reference bytes. It needs authenticated expected identities and sufficient signed metadata to demonstrate and troubleshoot reproduction. A successful comparison MUST be recorded in operator provenance before signing or production promotion. A ValidatedVariant must instead record its signed exception and distinct identities.

### 14.4 Operator runtime validation

The pipeline MUST provide the same versioned conformance suite and a documented, automatable procedure. After building its artifacts and instantiating a cluster, the operator runs that suite to validate the NKD conformance claim for its realization.

The result MUST be linked to the NKD recipe, builder profile, canonical input manifest, artifact release-set digest, exception identity when applicable, cluster identity, suite identity, and execution environment. This lets the operator demonstrate the technical result for its instantiated cluster without requiring NVIDIA to build or host the operator's artifacts.

Failed validation MUST block a conformant status and retain actionable evidence. The pipeline SHOULD distinguish a recipe defect from changed or unsupported operator inputs.

### 14.5 CNCF certification and marks

A technical Kubernetes conformance-suite pass and CNCF Certified Kubernetes status are separate claims. The former is test evidence; the latter also requires the CNCF conformance-program submission, review, and applicable terms.

An operator MAY factually report the exact suite, version, configuration, cluster, recipe, artifact identity, and result it ran. It MUST NOT describe its product or artifacts as Certified Kubernetes or use the Certified Kubernetes marks unless that operator and product are covered by a CNCF-approved submission and the applicable terms.

Whether an NVIDIA certification can cover byte-identical operator reproductions is a governance and legal dependency, not a technical inference. Until CNCF and NVIDIA Legal confirm that scope, the operator MUST either obtain its own certification or avoid certification and mark language. ValidatedVariants require independent review of certification scope.

Normative program references: CNCF Certified Kubernetes Conformance, [https://www.cncf.io/training/certification/software-conformance/](https://www.cncf.io/training/certification/software-conformance/); CNCF branding guidance, [https://www.cncf.io/kubecon-cloudnativecon-branding-guidelines/](https://www.cncf.io/kubecon-cloudnativecon-branding-guidelines/).

## 15\. Observability and audit {#15.-observability-and-audit}

The pipeline, NKE, and NodeWright MUST emit OpenTelemetry-compatible metrics, logs, traces, and state-change events.

Signals MUST expose:

- stage, state, start and completion time, and bounded retry count\
- recipe, pipeline, builder-profile, input-manifest, validation-vector, release-set, exception, cluster, and node identities\
- NVIDIA reference-build and operator reproduction results, including exact digest-match status and stable mismatch classification\
- validation and policy results with stable failure codes\
- rollout progress, health gates, interruption-budget use, and blocked workloads\
- drift and emergency-advisory state, including reconciliation deadlines\
- an audit trail for publication, build, promotion, deployment, exception, rollback, and reconciliation decisions

Logs MUST be actionable without secrets. Identical failures SHOULD yield stable error classification so operators can automate triage. Metric and attribute names follow OpenTelemetry semantic-convention naming: lowercase dot-delimited namespaces, snake\_case within a name component, and no unit suffix. Exporters MAY translate names for systems such as Prometheus without changing semantic identity.

### 15.1 Required metrics

The minimum portable metric set is:

| Metric | Instrument / unit | Required low-cardinality attributes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| nkd.build.run | Counter / {run} | nkd.builder.profile, nkd.result |
| nkd.build.duration | Histogram / s | nkd.builder.profile, nkd.stage, nkd.result |
| nkd.reproduction.status | Gauge / 1 | nkd.builder.profile, nkd.state={matched,mismatched,validated\_variant} |
| nkd.reproduction.mismatch | Counter / {mismatch} | nkd.mismatch.class, nkd.artifact.format |
| nkd.validation.run | Counter / {run} | nkd.validation.suite, nkd.result |
| nkd.fleet.drift.node | Gauge / {node} | nkd.drift.state, nkd.recipe.id |
| nkd.rollout.node | Gauge / {node} | nkd.rollout.state, nkd.recipe.id |
| nkd.emergency\_drift.deadline | Gauge / s | nkd.advisory.id, nkd.drift.state |

Status gauges use unit 1 and report value 1 for the current state. They MUST also report value 0 for every other member of the attribute's declared value set, in the same collection interval. Omitting non-current states makes a transition indistinguishable from a scrape gap on most backends and breaks alerting on state change; the value set is small and fixed, so the cardinality cost is bounded. nkd.emergency\_drift.deadline reports seconds remaining until the published reconciliation deadline; negative time is represented by UnsupportedDrift, not by an unbounded negative gauge.

### 15.2 Attribute and event contract

Stable attributes include nkd.recipe.id, nkd.recipe.digest, nkd.pipeline.digest, nkd.builder.profile, nkd.builder.profile.digest, nkd.validation\_vector.digest, nkd.artifact.id, nkd.artifact.format, nkd.overlay.digest, nkd.mismatch.class, nkd.mismatch.locus, nkd.mismatch.path, nkd.cluster.id, nkd.node.id, nkd.stage, nkd.result, error.type, and nkd.exception.id. Comparison and correlation MUST key on nkd.builder.profile.digest; nkd.builder.profile is a human-readable label only (Section 8.2.1). High-cardinality values such as artifact, cluster, node, path, block range, and trace identifiers belong in logs or traces unless a named metric explicitly requires them.

Logs use the OpenTelemetry Logs Data Model fields Timestamp, ObservedTimestamp, TraceId, SpanId, SeverityNumber, SeverityText, EventName, Body, Resource, InstrumentationScope, and Attributes. Stable event names include nkd.build.stage.completed, nkd.reproduction.mismatch, nkd.variant.approved, and nkd.drift.state\_changed; dynamic identifiers MUST be attributes, not event-name components.

### 15.3 Minimal mismatch event

The following JSON illustrates the required logical fields; transport encoding may differ:
