## 16\. Rollout plan and exit criteria {#16.-rollout-plan-and-exit-criteria}

### Phase 0: contract closure

- Resolve the P0 open decisions in [Section 19](#bookmark=id.7p2deocpwr93)\
- Define schemas, compatibility policy, support boundary, and required validation suites\
- Demonstrate two independent NVIDIA builds and one operator-equivalent build under the single declared v1 builder profile (Section 8.2.1), producing the same canonical artifact digests\
- Demonstrate fail-closed verification and end-to-end identity propagation\
- Publish the v1 overlay schema and demonstrate that a representative environment integration \- trust anchors, proxy, resolver, one agent \- lands as a declared overlay without voiding reproduction (Section 8.6)\
- Publish the reference content-manifest granularity and demonstrate that an injected divergence is locatable from the vector alone, with no access to reference bytes (Section 8.4.2)\
- Publish the builder-profile re-baseline SLA and grace window, and rehearse a host-image rotation against them (Section 8.2.2)

### Phase 1: DS9 reference adoption

- NVIDIA builds and validates a canonical reference set using only released interfaces\
- DS9 imports that same recipe, pipeline, and supported builder profile, reproduces the profile-specific canonical digests in DS9-owned infrastructure, and promotes the result to its registry\
- Exercise clean install, upgrade, rollback, and emergency reconciliation\
- Remove undocumented human steps from the common path

### Phase 2: external design partners

- Validate that operators can satisfy published builder profiles and run the pipeline in their own connected and air-gapped environments\
- Confirm that operators can reproduce the published conformance validation against their instantiated clusters\
- Measure first-attempt canonical digest match and time to diagnose mismatches across supported CI adapters\
- Measure onboarding effort, and measure how much customization pressure the declared overlay schema absorbs versus how much still forces fork status\
- Measure the pre-classified share of reproduction mismatches; a low share means the P0 self-service measure is carried by NVIDIA round trips (Section 8.4.1)\
- Confirm the support and incident-handoff model with real cases

### Phase 3: supported v1

- Publish immutable recipes, pipeline bundles, validation vectors, and CI adapters through the selected release channel\
- Publish compatibility, lifecycle, security, and support policies\
- Meet agreed reliability, patch-latency, upgrade, and self-service thresholds

## 17\. Success measures {#17.-success-measures}

The product P0 remains:

> A customer can successfully start NKE without contacting NVIDIA directly

The design must be read as satisfying this measure, not merely asserting it. Two paths in this document require an NVIDIA round trip by construction: a novel ValidatedVariant cause needs a signed exception, and a `provider-controlled` builder-profile re-baseline needs a republished profile. Both are bounded deliberately \- pre-classified causes are approved automatically on operator infrastructure (Section 8.4.1), and every recipe keeps an operator-controlled profile (Section 8.2.2) \- but neither is eliminated. The measure is therefore stated as: **an operator completes definition selection, build, reproduction, bootstrap, and first workload cluster without contacting NVIDIA, on the reproduction path and within the declared extension surface.** Contacts arising from novel-cause review or profile re-baselining are counted and reported separately rather than defined away.

That measure MUST be accompanied by:

- median and tail time from recipe selection to a ready Site Controller\
- unattended build, bootstrap, and first-workload-cluster success rates\
- NVIDIA reference-build repeatability and operator first-attempt canonical digest-match rates by supported builder profile\
- median and tail time to diagnose and correct a reproduction mismatch\
- operator conformance-validation completion and pass rates\
- time from an applicable critical fix to a published recipe and operator convergence\
- normal upgrade completion, rollback, and blocked-rollout rates\
- fleet convergence and unauthorized-drift rates\
- support contacts per deployment, classified by failed stage and owner, with novel-cause review and profile re-baseline counted as distinct categories\
- percentage of external operators completing the pipeline without NVIDIA intervention\
- share of reproduction mismatches resolved by pre-classified cause versus signed exception\
- share of operator environment integrations absorbed by the declared overlay schema versus forced into fork status\
- elapsed time from a provider host-image change to a republished builder profile, against the declared re-baseline SLA\
- adoption and sustained use by external operators, not only internal fleets

Numeric targets and measurement windows are P0 product decisions before v1 exit.

## 18\. Risks and trade-offs {#18.-risks-and-trade-offs}

| Risk | Consequence | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Operators reject the build-pipeline burden | NKD solves the integration problem but fails the delivery-model test. | Validate with external design partners; measure intervention; define a trigger for reference artifacts. |
| CI adapters accumulate build logic | GitHub, GitLab, and Jenkins produce different artifacts while claiming to run NKD. | Keep all semantics in one hermetic engine; publish explicit builder profiles; test each adapter/profile pair against its own digest vector. |
| Operator-controlled inputs weaken reproducibility | Builds diverge while appearing to represent the same recipe. | Pin every canonical input and host dependency in the builder profile; separate the operator envelope; classify any substitution as a variant. |
| Withheld reference bytes make mismatch diagnosis opaque | Operators can detect a failure but cannot explain it. | Publish signed content manifests, SBOMs, normalized metadata, stable error codes, and a deterministic diff tool \- at the granularity fixed in Section 8.4.2, which is the binding constraint, not the tooling. |
| Withholding is defended as a liability reduction it does not deliver | Section 12 already assigns NVIDIA the full definition, security, and conformance obligation; an overstated rationale collapses under customer or legal scrutiny and reopens the delivery decision late. | State the avoided obligations exactly (Section 4.1); keep operator-facing material to hosting, binary-artifact CVE SLA, and packaging-matrix scope. |
| A provider-controlled runner image rotates | Fail-closed preflight halts every operator on that profile at once, with no operator-side remedy. | Maintain an operator-controlled profile per recipe; hard-fail only fields demonstrated to change output; publish a re-baseline SLA and grace window (Section 8.2.2). |
| No declared extension surface | Ordinary environment integration forces fork status; operators quietly fork or walk away. | Publish and version the overlay schema; treat unmet need as a schema gap to close, not as fork tolerance (Section 8.6). |
| Release cadence exceeds operator build and rollout capacity | Operators fall behind on security convergence, or stop rebuilding and drift. | Publish expected cadence per release class, a batching policy, and the maximum supported interval on a superseded recipe (Section 9.6). |
| The same implementation builds and validates | One defect can create the artifact and incorrectly bless it. | Isolate or independently implement the verifier and run runtime conformance as a separate gate. |
| The reference build passes but an operator's cluster does not | The NKD conformance claim is misunderstood as proof for untested artifacts. | Ship the exact suite and bind operator results to recipe, artifacts, and cluster identity. |
| Product ownership is fragmented across AICR, Skysmith, package builder, NKE, and NodeWright | Integration gaps become customer-visible handoffs. | Assign one end-to-end release owner and gate releases on the complete lifecycle. |
| Immutable rollout lacks spare GPU capacity | Security and version convergence stalls or interrupts workloads. | Preflight capacity and workload constraints; expose blocked rollouts; define exception policy. |
| Emergency mutation becomes permanent | Fleet state diverges from the recipe and audit claims become false. | Record expiring drift, alert before expiry, and require replacement from a reconciled recipe. |
| “Not a distro” is interpreted as “no NVIDIA responsibility” | Support disputes and slow incident response. | Publish the responsibility matrix, lifecycle, compatibility, and security-response policies with v1. |
| Air-gapped trust metadata becomes stale | Operators cannot validate new recipes or revocations. | Define signed offline bundles, freshness policy, and controlled evidence export before broad adoption. |
| Byte identity is implied across heterogeneous CI hosts | A supported CI brand produces nondeterministic artifacts or an impossible guarantee. | Scope the guarantee to signed builder profiles keyed by digest; preflight host properties; publish a reference digest vector for each profile; cap v1 at one declared profile (Section 8.2.1). |
| Supported-profile count grows faster than validation capacity | Per-release validation cost becomes unpredictable and Phase 0 never closes. | One declared v1 profile; demand-driven expansion only, each with a published incremental validation cost (Section 8.2.1). |
| ValidatedVariant becomes a routine bypass | Exact reproduction erodes and support/certification claims become ambiguous. | Limit eligibility to proven representation differences; require all suites, signed approval, distinct identity, support scope, and expiry. Remove the largest structural source by making RAW canonical and QCOW2 a derived envelope (Section 8.3.1), and keep repeat causes out of review via pre-classification (Section 8.4.1). |
| Conformance result is presented as CNCF certification | Operators misuse certification language or marks. | Separate technical evidence from CNCF program status and require approved submission/terms before certification claims or marks. |

## 19\. Open decisions {#19.-open-decisions}

### P0: required before supported external release

1. **Identity and versioning:** define the relationship among semantic version, recipe digest, pipeline bundle, input manifest, validation vector, release-set digest, overlay digest, and SBOM identity.\
2. **Distribution and discovery:** choose the signed channel for recipes, pipeline bundles, CI adapters, validation vectors, lifecycle metadata, and revocations; define mirroring behavior.\
3. **Support contract:** approve supported parameters, builder-profile lifecycle, ValidatedVariant scope and approval authority, forks, response ownership, EmergencyDrift/UnsupportedDrift SLA, and incident-liability boundaries.\
4. **Compatibility contract:** publish the NKE, Kubernetes, AICR, OS, kernel, architecture, firmware, driver, and upgrade-edge matrix.\
5. **Canonicalization implementation:** encode the format-specific boundaries in schema and verifier tests, including RAW logical ranges, ISO metadata, package signatures, UUIDs, the deterministic RAW-to-envelope conversion step, and operator envelopes. The v1 semantic boundary \- RAW canonical, QCOW2/VMDK/VHD derived \- is decided in Section 8.3.1; what remains is encoding and test coverage.\
6. **Reference content-manifest granularity:** fix the block size, manifest schema, and any redaction for the published validation vector, and confirm the resulting disclosure is acceptable against the obligations Section 4.1 says withholding actually avoids. This is the binding constraint on whether Section 13.1 triage is executable at all (Section 8.4.2).\
7. **Extension surface:** publish the initial overlay schema \- which configuration domains are extensible, their constraints, their application point, and how overlay digests enter release-set and node-reported identity (Section 8.6).\
8. **Builder-profile lifecycle:** declare the single v1 profile and its host-control class, the hard-fail versus advisory field split, the re-baseline SLA, the grace window, and the deprecation overlap policy (Sections 8.2.1, 8.2.2).\
9. **Release cadence:** publish expected cadence per release class, the batching policy, and the maximum interval an operator may remain on a superseded recipe while supported (Section 9.6).\
10. **Air-gapped flow:** define mirrored inputs, offline trust metadata, revocation freshness, and evidence export. Promoted from P1: Section 11.2 makes air-gapped verification semantics a MUST, and Phase 2 exit requires operators to run the pipeline in disconnected environments, so it cannot be deferred past v1.\
11. **Conformance and certification governance:** select exact suite versions, evidence format, operator promotion policy, CNCF submission owner, certification scope for reproduced artifacts, ValidatedVariant treatment, mark usage, and Legal approval. The technical claim and operator-verification workflow are defined in Section 14\.\
12. **CVE policy:** define severity thresholds, publication SLA, emergency authorization, drift expiry, enforcement owner, and exact commercial terms for UnsupportedDrift. The technical state transition and default support behavior are defined in Sections 9.5 and 12\.\
13. **Bootstrap and rollback:** specify the Site Controller bootstrap API, trust root, readiness contract, state backup, and supported rollback procedure.\
14. **AICR interface:** confirm AICR as the foundational runtime-recipe substrate and define the versioned contract between the NKD distribution recipe and AICR runtime profile.\
15. **Independent verifier and variant authority:** decide whether verification is a second implementation or isolated verifier, name the NVIDIA authority that can sign a ValidatedVariant exception, and define how a novel cause is promoted to pre-classified (Section 8.4.1).

### P1: required for broad adoption

16. **Capacity policy:** define preflight calculation and operator-facing behavior when spare GPU capacity or workload interruption budgets prevent replacement.\
17. **Reference artifacts:** establish the evidence threshold that would trigger NVIDIA-published reference images and their support level.\
18. **Builder-profile expansion:** define the demand evidence and published incremental validation cost required to add a profile beyond the single v1 profile.\
19. **Service objectives:** set targets and measurement windows for the metrics in [Section 17](#bookmark=id.mi5zu1jyhaga).\
20. **Component readiness:** publish implementation and ownership status for recipe schema, builder-profile schema and preflight, pipeline engine, CI adapters, Skysmith, package builder, reproduction verifier and diff tools, overlay tooling, validation tooling, NodeWright, NKE, and their APIs.

## Appendix A: Why NKD is not a distribution {#appendix-a:-why-nkd-is-not-a-distribution}

A conventional distribution such as RKE2 typically carries source patches, rebuilds components, packages images and binaries, embeds configuration opinions, validates the release, and publishes installable artifacts. Its vendor owns the artifact supply chain, release endpoints, packaging matrix, conformance posture, and binary security response.

NKD injects its opinions into a signed recipe and reproducible pipeline. NVIDIA builds and validates canonical reference artifacts but stops before distributing them:

| Stage | Conventional distribution | NKD v1 |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Select and configure components | Vendor | NVIDIA distribution recipe, with AICR foundational to the accelerated-runtime profile |
| Build and package | Vendor builds release artifacts | NVIDIA builds profile-specific internal canonical artifacts; the operator reproduces them with the same released recipe, pipeline, inputs, and builder profile. |
| Validate compatibility and conformance | Vendor validates its artifacts | NVIDIA validates its canonical artifacts; the operator verifies exact byte identity or a signed ValidatedVariant exception, then runs the same runtime suites. |
| Publish | Vendor publishes installable bytes | NVIDIA publishes recipe, pipeline, digests, provenance, and evidence-but not artifact bytes |
| Sign production artifacts | Vendor | Operator, after canonical reproduction succeeds |
| Install and operate | Customer installs vendor bytes | NKE consumes operator-built, verified artifacts |
| Sustain | Vendor publishes replacement bytes | NVIDIA publishes a new recipe, reference digest set, and evidence; operator reproduces and rolls out |

The distinction is about the delivery and ownership boundary, not the absence of vendor obligations. Because NVIDIA defines and validates the configuration, NKD still requires an explicit compatibility contract, security response, lifecycle policy, and support model.

## Appendix B: Minimal contract examples {#appendix-b:-minimal-contract-examples}

### B.1 NKD distribution recipe

This non-normative YAML shows the minimum linkage among recipe, NKE compatibility, AICR, pipeline, builder profile, canonical inputs, and validation vector. Production schemas MUST use immutable, verified references.

```
apiVersion: nkd.nvidia.com/v1alpha1
kind: DistributionRecipe
metadata:
  name: nkd-1.0.0
spec:
  nke:
    versions: ["1.0.x"]
  kubernetes:
    version: "1.35.1"
  aicrProfile:
    id: "aicr-hgx-b200-v1"
    digest: "sha256:<aicr-profile>"
  pipeline:
    digest: "sha256:<pipeline-engine>"
  # v1 declares exactly one supported builder profile (Section 8.2.1).
  # The digest is the identity; the id is a human-readable label.
  builderProfiles:
    - id: "selfhosted-ubuntu-24.04-amd64-v1"
      digest: "sha256:<builder-profile>"
      hostControl: operator-controlled        # or: provider-controlled
      validationVector: "oci://nvcr.io/nkd/vectors/nkd-1.0.0-selfhosted@sha256:<vector>"
  inputs:
    baseImage: "oci://nvcr.io/nkd/base@sha256:<base-image>"
    repositorySnapshot: "oci://nvcr.io/nkd/repos@sha256:<snapshot>"
  artifactPolicy:
    # RAW is the canonical, byte-reproduced OS artifact (Section 8.3.1).
    osImage:
      canonical: {format: raw, canonicalization: raw-lba-v1}
      # Derived envelopes are converted AFTER reproduction and are verified
      # by logical-disk digest only; the container file is never compared.
      deliveryEnvelopes:
        - {format: qcow2, converter: "qemu-img@<pinned>", canonicalization: envelope-v1}
    packages: {format: tar, canonicalization: package-bundle-v1}
  # Bounded operator extension surface (Section 8.6). Anything outside this
  # schema is a fork, not a variant.
  extensionSurface:
    overlaySchema: "nkd.nvidia.com/overlay/v1alpha1"
    domains: [trustAnchors, proxy, resolver, timeSources, agents, authn]
    forbidden: [kubernetes, kubelet, containerRuntime, acceleratedStack]
  validation:
    kubernetesConformance: "sonobuoy-v<version>"
    nkeIntegration: "nke-validation-v<version>"
    # The overlaid instantiation is what gets validated, not the bare image.
    target: overlaid
```

### B.2 Validation vector

The vector is signed as a whole and binds one builder profile to expected artifacts and evidence.

```
apiVersion: nkd.nvidia.com/v1alpha1
kind: ValidationVector
metadata:
  name: nkd-1.0.0-selfhosted-ubuntu-24.04-amd64-v1
spec:
  recipeDigest: "sha256:<recipe>"
  pipelineDigest: "sha256:<pipeline-engine>"
  builderProfile:
    id: "selfhosted-ubuntu-24.04-amd64-v1"
    digest: "sha256:<builder-profile>"        # authoritative identity
    hostControl: operator-controlled
  inputManifestDigest: "sha256:<inputs>"
  artifacts:
    - id: "os-raw-amd64"
      role: canonical
      format: raw
      logicalContentDigest: "sha256:<logical-lba-stream>"
      contentManifestDigest: "sha256:<filesystem-manifest>"
      # Granularity is what makes mismatch diagnosable without reference
      # bytes (Section 8.4.2). Published, not implied.
      manifestGranularity:
        blockRangeDigests: {blockSize: 1048576, digest: "sha256:<block-map>"}
        pathManifest: {fields: [path, mode, uid, gid, size, digest]}
    - id: "kubernetes-packages-amd64"
      role: canonical
      format: tar
      deliveryDigest: "sha256:<bundle-bytes>"
      contentManifestDigest: "sha256:<package-manifest>"
      manifestGranularity:
        entryManifest: {fields: [path, mode, uid, gid, size, digest]}
  # Derived envelopes are not compared as bytes; they must decode to the
  # canonical RAW logical digest above (Section 8.3.1).
  deliveryEnvelopes:
    - id: "os-qcow2-amd64"
      derivedFrom: "os-raw-amd64"
      format: qcow2
      converter: "qemu-img@<pinned>"
  # Causes the operator may clear automatically, without an NVIDIA round
  # trip, when the predicate holds and all gates pass (Section 8.4.1).
  preClassifiedCauses:
    - id: "NKD-PC-0001"
      class: NONDETERMINISTIC_METADATA
      predicate: "divergence confined to /etc/machine-id, zero-length at first boot"
      expires: "<date>"
  evidence:
    sbomDigest: "sha256:<sbom>"
    provenanceDigest: "sha256:<provenance>"
    kubernetesConformanceDigest: "sha256:<conformance-results>"
    nkeValidationDigest: "sha256:<nke-results>"
  signature: "<detached-or-envelope-signature>"
```

## Appendix C: Architecture Diagram Source

```
flowchart TB
    subgraph NV["NVIDIA release domain - publishes the definition and the evidence"]
        R["Signed NKD distribution recipe<br/>+ pipeline engine bundle"]
        P["Supported builder profile<br/>signed, immutable"]
        RB["NVIDIA reference build"]
        RA["Internal reference artifacts<br/><b>NOT DISTRIBUTED</b>"]
        VV["Signed validation vector<br/>expected digests · content manifests<br/>SBOM · provenance · conformance"]
        R --> P --> RB --> RA --> VV
    end

    subgraph OP["Operator supply-chain domain - reproduces, signs, promotes"]
        IN["Mirror pinned inputs<br/>exact content, no substitution"]
        AD["Thin CI adapter"]
        OB["Operator build<br/>same engine, same profile"]
        CMP{"Reproduction verifier<br/>delivery + logical content"}
        FAIL["Fail closed<br/>unpromoted candidate"]
        SIGN["Operator signature +<br/>registry envelope"]
        PROM["Scan · attest · promote"]
        IN --> AD --> OB --> CMP
        CMP -->|"exact match → Reproduced"| SIGN
        CMP -->|"eligible cause → gated ValidatedVariant"| SIGN
        CMP -->|"any other cause"| FAIL
        SIGN --> PROM
    end

    subgraph RT["Operator runtime domain"]
        REG["Operator registry"] --> NKEB["NKE + NodeWright"] --> CL["Validated clusters"]
    end

    R -->|"released contracts"| IN
    P -->|"preflight"| AD
    VV -->|"expected identities only, never bytes"| CMP
    PROM --> REG
```
